public_rationale: The ordinary claim of buildout constraints is supported. Wood Mackenzie identifies transformer deficits, electrical-steel supply problems and specialist labor constraints. The construction survey independently establishes widespread hiring difficulties. European steel-factory underutilization qualifies the geographic breadth: these records do not show that every country or steel grade was in shortage.
limitations: Support is strongest for American transformers and construction labor.
The evidence establishes procurement constraints, not uniform worldwide physical scarcity.
The selected annual period does not establish daily conditions immediately before publication.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The data center buildout faces shortages of electrical steel, transformers and skilled labor.

statement.excerpt: We’ve already got a shortage in the electrical grade steel and transformers required to expand America’s (and the world’s) power grid, we’ve already got a shortage of skilled labor required to build that power (and data centers in general), and we’re moving massive amounts of heavy shit around a large patch of land using thousands of people, which will cost a lot of gas.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that material and workforce shortages constrain the buildout, not that every project or country lacks these inputs.
Electrical steel means the transformer-grade material discussed in the surrounding power-grid context.
Use calendar 2025, the latest completed annual reporting period before the post, for the cross-industry observation. This does not establish conditions on every day through March 10.
Assess the supplied proposition about shortages; the sentence’s unquantified fuel-cost prediction is outside that proposition.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous industry research identifies transformer and electrical-steel supply constraints, while construction evidence identifies difficulty obtaining skilled workers.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence shows adequate availability across the named inputs, or establishes that the alleged shortages had ended during the target period.

evidence.locator: Sections The root causes and Key market developments
evidence.explanation: The research identifies current transformer deficits and connects demand growth to data centers. Its discussion of raw-material shortages identifies electrical steel as a key constraint, alongside specialist manufacturing labor.

evidence.publisher: National Center for Construction Education and Research
evidence.explanation: The survey summary reports hiring difficulties at 92 percent of companies and identifies a skilled workforce shortage. This supports the construction-labor component, although the published summary covers construction broadly.

evidence.excerpt: substantial underutilization of the European production facilities.
evidence.locator: Second substantive paragraph of December 11 press release
evidence.explanation: The manufacturer reported rising low-priced imports and idle European capacity. This qualifies any suggestion of a uniform worldwide steel shortage, but does not establish adequate availability for American transformer manufacturers.
